question: A 17-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his father because of fever, congestion, and malaise for the past 2 days. He reports a sensation of pressure over his nose and cheeks. Over the past year, he has had an intermittent cough productive of green sputum and lately has noticed some streaks of blood in the sputum. He has had over 10 episodes of sinusitis, all of which were successfully treated with antibiotics. There is no family history of serious illness. The patient's vaccinations are up-to-date. His temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 120/80 mm Hg. Physical examination shows tenderness to palpation over both cheeks. Crackles and rhonchi are heard on auscultation of the chest. Cardiac examination shows an absence of heart sounds along the left lower chest. Which of the following additional findings is most likely in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Chronic sinusitis -> recurrent episodes of sinusitis -> possible chronic respiratory infections -> possible bronchiectasis -> increased sweat chloride levels -> 70% CHAIN: Chronic sinusitis -> recurrent episodes of sinusitis -> possible chronic respiratory infections -> possible bronchiectasis -> increased sweat chloride levels -> Defective interleukin-2 receptor gamma chain -> 70%
enhanced_information: The most likely additional finding in this patient is increased sweat chloride levels, indicating a possible diagnosis of cystic fibrosis. The presence of chronic sinusitis, recurrent respiratory infections, bronchiectasis, and the potential link to defective interleukin-2 receptor gamma chain support this conclusion.
analysis: The core medical principle here is to consider the constellation of symptoms and the patient's history to arrive at a likely diagnosis. The patient's history of recurrent sinusitis, respiratory infections, bronchiectasis, and the potential link to defective interleukin-2 receptor gamma chain point towards cystic fibrosis. The enhanced information provided supports the likelihood of increased sweat chloride levels in this patient, which is a key diagnostic feature of cystic fibrosis.
